title: Long SKHY — SK Hynix ADR Debut, HBM4 Pure Play, 7x Oversubscribed
entry: Evaluate at July 10 Nasdaq debut open. Entry framework per institutional demand signal: ≥$175 (≥10.6% above $158.26 indicative) = full 5% allocation — confirms pricing absorbed with premium intact; $165–$175 = 50% starter position at open, add if it holds $165 through first hour; <$165 = demand miss — do not enter, wait for a secondary base formation (3-day consolidation above $155) before reassessing. Do not chase intraday above $185 on debut day (debut spikes often retrace 5-10% before the secondary base forms).
stop_loss: $140 daily close — implies either (a) debut-day institutional sellers overwhelm the 7x oversubscribed demand signal, breaking the supply/demand balance; (b) HBM4 demand news between pricing and MSCI inclusion cycle turns negative (Rubin delay, NVDA capex reduction); or (c) Nasdaq-100 decline >3% on debut day creates index-level selling pressure that overrides the demand thesis. At $140 the HBM4 pure-play premium is structurally broken regardless of subsequent catalysts.
targets: $175 — debut session closes at or above pricing premium (>10.6% above $158.26 indicative); QQQ-equivalent forced buying from Nasdaq-100 passive funds absorbs the first two weeks of selling; +10.6% from indicative; take 30% of position on first close above $175

$195 — 3-week post-listing base established; first MSCI Emerging Markets and Standard Korea index inclusion window approached (typically 2-3 quarters post-listing but accelerated consideration at this offering scale); institutional roadshow investors complete their ADR allocation; SK Hynix reports first US-listed quarterly earnings confirming HBM4 revenue trajectory; +23.2% from indicative

$230 — MSCI World inclusion trigger window open; Rubin GPU production ramp cited in SK Hynix guidance; HBM4 ASP revised upward above $500/stack consensus; SK Hynix 12-layer HBM4E sample transition to mass production announced; +45.4% from indicative
risk_reward: 1:1.5 at Target 1 (from $165 entry); 1:3.8 at Target 2; 1:8.0 at Target 3
catalyst: SK Hynix $28B Nasdaq ADR pricing tonight (July 9) with 7x oversubscription — $171.5B in orders from approximately 1,000 institutional investors including $7B cornerstone commitments from Baillie Gifford, Coatue, and SAP. The SKHY listing creates the first US-listed pure-play HBM4 vehicle: 100% revenue exposure to high-bandwidth memory sold to AI inference/training clusters (NVDA Blackwell/Rubin, GOOGL TPU, AMD MI series). Debut July 10 under SKHY on Nasdaq Global Select Market.
thesis:
The SKHY ADR is the most institutionally validated AI-cycle offering of 2026. A 7x oversubscription with $171.5B in total orders — the largest foreign ADR demand in history — is not sentiment: it is approximately 1,000 institutions completing a week-long due diligence roadshow and then writing checks. They have vetted the HBM4 supply chain, the Rubin GPU production ramp, and the SK Hynix competitive position (58% global HBM market share per UBS), and voted with $171.5B to participate. The bear cases — Kyber NVL144 PCB delay, FOMC hike risk, Iran geopolitical drag — were all live during the bookbuild. Institutions priced in and still bought 7x the offering. That is the clearest demand signal for the AI memory cycle available.

SK Hynix offers something unavailable elsewhere in US markets: direct, pure-play exposure to HBM4 revenue without the dilution of a diversified semiconductor company. NVDA carries fabrication risk and competitive exposure. TSM carries Taiwan geopolitical risk and foundry margin structure. AVGO blends AI ASIC revenue with networking. SKHY is 100% HBM4 and DRAM — the exact node where AI demand is concentrating. SK Hynix has been the primary qualified HBM4 supplier for NVDA's Blackwell generation; NVDA Gate 3 (H200 China approval July 8) confirms that the Rubin/Vera Rubin Ultra generation — requiring HBM4 at scale — has a market.

The MSCI inclusion clock is the structural tailwind that extends beyond the debut. MSCI Emerging Markets and Standard Korea index inclusion typically begins 2-3 quarters post-listing for large-cap foreign ADRs; at $28B offering size and market cap >$1T (KRW equivalent), SKHY would qualify for accelerated review. Passive inflows on MSCI inclusion are estimated at $12-15B, dwarfing the IPO offering size itself. That future inflow is not in the debut price.

The entry framework is conditional by design: if SKHY trades below $165 at debut (implying weak pricing), the thesis weakens because a demand miss below indicative levels would suggest the 7x oversubscription was driven by soft commitments. Above $175, the demand signal is confirmed by market price. The stop at $140 provides a 10.6-15.2% buffer from the entry zone that should absorb normal debut-day volatility while protecting against structural demand failure.
bull_case: SKHY prices above the indicative $158.26 tonight — reports suggest $165-175 range given demand — and opens July 10 with strong buying. The KOSPI's +3.7% reversal on July 9 (its deepest two-session recovery in 2026) is powered by SK Hynix KRX +7.76%, validating that Korean institutional money is also buying the HBM4 demand signal. By the third week of trading, first MSCI consideration language appears in research; by week 6, SK Hynix reports its first Nasdaq-listed earnings with HBM4 volume and ASP guidance that exceeds the $500/stack consensus, driving SKHY to $195+.
bear_case: SKHY debuts below indicative ($158.26) — possibly at $150-155 — on 'soft commitment' unwinding from investors who signed up for the roadshow but back out at pricing. The 7x oversubscription was real but at the $158 indicative level; the final pricing (tonight) might disappoint if bookrunners price too aggressively. Alternatively, June CPI on July 14 prints ≥4.5%, re-igniting the September FOMC hike and compressing all growth multiples including SKHY's. A debut below $155 and continuation below $150 would suggest the demand signal was institutional posturing rather than committed capital.
invalidation: $140 SKHY daily close; OR SKHY debuts below $155 and closes the debut session below $155 (demand-miss signal, do not enter); OR June CPI July 14 prints ≥4.5% triggering September hike probability above 85% (growth multiple compression across all AI semis); OR NVDA announces Rubin/Vera Rubin Ultra HBM4 production delay beyond Q4 2026 (removes the primary HBM4 demand catalyst).

outcome.outcome_label: Target 1 ($175) and approaching Target 2 ($195) — closed at $193.92
outcome.note: SKHY debuted on Nasdaq July 10 at $170 open with strong institutional demand. Target 1 ($175) was hit within the first trading session as expected from the 7x oversubscribed demand signal. By July 15 SKHY reached $193.92, within $1.08 of Target 2 ($195). ASML's Q2 beat-and-raise earnings (€9.3B revenue, guide raised to €43–45B) on July 15 reinforced the AI semiconductor supercycle thesis. Closing the position near Target 2 to lock in +27.3% from the $152.35 reference price (+14.1% from $170 debut entry). The MSCI inclusion structural tailwind remains but further upside captured in the new ASML long opportunity.
